text: Each RPS channel shall execute its protection logic cyclically with a fixed scan period k_Scan_Period; inputs are sampled once at the start of each scan.

A trip function shall be placed in the tripped state, and its pre-trip alarm actuated, without intentional delay whenever an error of the function is present. The errors of a function are: a processor module error (f_Module_Error = 1), a channel error (f_Channel_Error = 1), an invalid process input of the function, and for functions using core protection calculator signals the loss of the CPC data link.  An input used only by an operating-bypass permissive is not a process input: while it is invalid the permissive is not satisfied (SYS-GEN-09).
Each analog process input f_S shall be declared invalid when it lies outside its valid range [k_S_Valid_Min, k_S_Valid_Max].

At start-up every trip and pre-trip output shall be in the tripped state and every operating bypass shall be removed; an output shall leave the tripped state only in a scan in which no error of the function is present.  When an error that did not interrupt a process trip clears (or at start-up) while the trip (pre-trip) condition is present and the function is not in operating bypass, the output shall remain tripped; it shall become a process trip if the condition persists for the trip (pre-trip) delay, and shall return to NORMAL as soon as the condition clears.  A process trip interrupted by an error is governed by SYS-GEN-07.
Trip and pre-trip outputs shall use de-energize-to-trip polarity: 0 = TRIP/PRETRIP, 1 = NORMAL.

A trip (pre-trip) caused by a process condition shall be generated when, and only when, the condition has persisted continuously for the trip (pre-trip) delay of the function.  Process conditions are evaluated only in scans in which no error of the function is present; persistence is measured over consecutive such scans in which the function is not in operating bypass, so an error or an active operating bypass interrupts it.  When a bypass is removed while the condition is present, the trip follows after the delay.

Once tripped (pre-tripped) by a process condition, a trip function shall remain tripped until the process variable has recovered past the trip (pre-trip) setpoint by more than the reset hysteresis, or the function is placed in operating bypass.  A process trip is held through errors of the function; its release condition is evaluated only in scans without an error of the function.
Each trip function shall provide a pre-trip alarm generated at a setpoint closer to normal operating conditions than the trip setpoint.

An operating bypass shall be established only by an operator initiation, i.e. a press of its initiation pushbutton made while its permissive condition is satisfied; a pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall not establish a bypass.  A permissive is not satisfied while its input is invalid.  The bypass shall be removed automatically, without operator action, in the first scan in which the permissive is no longer satisfied.  While bypassed, the function's process trip and pre-trip are inhibited; trips caused by errors are not inhibited.
The status of each trip channel bypass switch shall be transmitted with the channel's trip outputs to the coincidence processors.
For each trip function the coincidence processor shall generate a coincidence trip when at least two of the four channels are tripped (2-out-of-4).

A channel with a trip channel bypass requested shall be excluded from the vote of that function (2-out-of-3 logic), provided no other channel requests bypass of the same function; if two or more channels request bypass of the same function, all those requests shall be ignored (2-out-of-4 logic retained).
A channel whose data link has failed shall be counted as tripped for every trip function for which it is not validly bypassed.
The coincidence processor shall generate the reactor trip initiation signal when the coincidence trip of any trip function is present.

The RPS shall generate a Variable Overpower trip when the excore linear nuclear power (f_NPWR_LIN) rises to or above the variable trip setpoint h_VOPT_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above h_VOPT_Trip_SP - k_VOPT_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_VOPT_Trip_SP shall track f_NPWR_LIN + k_VOPT_Band limited to [k_VOPT_SP_Min, k_VOPT_SP_Max].  It shall follow decreasing power without delay and shall increase at no more than k_VOPT_SP_Rate, so that a rapid power increase produces a trip.  At start-up it shall be initialised from the first valid input.

The RPS shall generate a High Logarithmic Power Level trip when the excore logarithmic nuclear power (f_NPWR_LOG) rises to or above k_LOGP_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_LOGP_HI_Pretrip_SP.
The High Logarithmic Power Level trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_LOGP_HI_OB_Ini) while f_NPWR_LOG >= k_LOGP_HI_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a High Local Power Density (CPC) trip when the core protection calculator reports a local power density trip (f_LPD_HI_Trip_In = 0), and a pre-trip alarm when it reports a pre-trip (f_LPD_HI_Pretrip_In = 0).  Loss of the CPC data link (f_CPC_Link_Error = 1) shall be treated as an error.
The High Local Power Density (CPC) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_LPD_HI_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).

The RPS shall generate a Low DNBR (CPC) trip when the core protection calculator reports a departure from nucleate boiling ratio trip (f_DNBR_LO_Trip_In = 0), and a pre-trip alarm when it reports a pre-trip (f_DNBR_LO_Pretrip_In = 0).  Loss of the CPC data link (f_CPC_Link_Error = 1) shall be treated as an error.
The Low DNBR (CPC) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_DNBR_LO_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).

The RPS shall generate a High Pressurizer Pressure trip when the pressurizer pressure (wide range) (f_PZR_P) rises to or above k_PZR_P_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_PZR_P_HI_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a Low Pressurizer Pressure trip when the pressurizer pressure (wide range) (f_PZR_P) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP + k_PZR_P_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_PZR_P_LO_Trip_SP shall be k_PZR_P_LO_SP_Max at start-up.  Each operator actuation of the setpoint reset pushbutton f_PZR_P_LO_SP_Reset shall lower the setpoint to f_PZR_P - k_PZR_P_LO_Band, but not below k_PZR_P_LO_SP_Min; a reset shall never raise the setpoint and one actuation shall produce at most one reduction.  A pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall produce no reduction, an actuation made while f_PZR_P is invalid shall be ignored, and the setpoint shall hold its value while f_PZR_P is invalid.  The setpoint shall rise automatically so that it is never more than k_PZR_P_LO_Band below f_PZR_P, up to k_PZR_P_LO_SP_Max.
The Low Pressurizer Pressure trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_PZR_P_LO_OB_Ini) while f_PZR_P < k_PZR_P_LO_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a Low Steam Generator 1 Water Level trip when the steam generator 1 water level (narrow range) (f_SG1_L) falls to or below k_SG1_L_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below k_SG1_L_LO_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a Low Steam Generator 2 Water Level trip when the steam generator 2 water level (narrow range) (f_SG2_L) falls to or below k_SG2_L_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below k_SG2_L_LO_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a High Steam Generator 1 Water Level trip when the steam generator 1 water level (narrow range) (f_SG1_L) rises to or above k_SG1_L_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_SG1_L_HI_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a High Steam Generator 2 Water Level trip when the steam generator 2 water level (narrow range) (f_SG2_L) rises to or above k_SG2_L_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_SG2_L_HI_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a Low Steam Generator 1 Pressure trip when the steam generator 1 pressure (f_SG1_P) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_SG1_P_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_SG1_P_LO_Trip_SP + k_SG1_P_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_SG1_P_LO_Trip_SP shall be k_SG1_P_LO_SP_Max at start-up.  Each operator actuation of the setpoint reset pushbutton f_SG1_P_LO_SP_Reset shall lower the setpoint to f_SG1_P - k_SG1_P_LO_Band, but not below k_SG1_P_LO_SP_Min; a reset shall never raise the setpoint and one actuation shall produce at most one reduction.  A pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall produce no reduction, an actuation made while f_SG1_P is invalid shall be ignored, and the setpoint shall hold its value while f_SG1_P is invalid.  The setpoint shall rise automatically so that it is never more than k_SG1_P_LO_Band below f_SG1_P, up to k_SG1_P_LO_SP_Max.
The Low Steam Generator 1 Pressure trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_SG1_P_LO_OB_Ini) while f_SG1_P < k_SG1_P_LO_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a Low Steam Generator 2 Pressure trip when the steam generator 2 pressure (f_SG2_P) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_SG2_P_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_SG2_P_LO_Trip_SP + k_SG2_P_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_SG2_P_LO_Trip_SP shall be k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Max at start-up.  Each operator actuation of the setpoint reset pushbutton f_SG2_P_LO_SP_Reset shall lower the setpoint to f_SG2_P - k_SG2_P_LO_Band, but not below k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Min; a reset shall never raise the setpoint and one actuation shall produce at most one reduction.  A pushbutton held or stuck in the pressed state (including at start-up) shall produce no reduction, an actuation made while f_SG2_P is invalid shall be ignored, and the setpoint shall hold its value while f_SG2_P is invalid.  The setpoint shall rise automatically so that it is never more than k_SG2_P_LO_Band below f_SG2_P, up to k_SG2_P_LO_SP_Max.
The Low Steam Generator 2 Pressure trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_SG2_P_LO_OB_Ini) while f_SG2_P < k_SG2_P_LO_OB_Perm.

The RPS shall generate a High Containment Pressure trip when the containment pressure (f_CTMT_P) rises to or above k_CTMT_P_HI_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it rises to or above k_CTMT_P_HI_Pretrip_SP.

The RPS shall generate a Low Reactor Coolant Flow (SG1 loop) trip when the reactor coolant flow, SG1 loop (from SG differential pressure) (f_SG1_F) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_SG1_F_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_SG1_F_LO_Trip_SP + k_SG1_F_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_SG1_F_LO_Trip_SP shall track f_SG1_F - k_SG1_F_LO_Band limited to [k_SG1_F_LO_SP_Min, k_SG1_F_LO_SP_Max].  It shall follow increasing flow without delay and shall decrease at no more than k_SG1_F_LO_SP_Rate, so that a rapid flow reduction produces a trip.  At start-up it shall be initialised from the first valid input.
The Low Reactor Coolant Flow (SG1 loop) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_SG1_F_LO_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).

The RPS shall generate a Low Reactor Coolant Flow (SG2 loop) trip when the reactor coolant flow, SG2 loop (from SG differential pressure) (f_SG2_F) falls to or below the variable trip setpoint h_SG2_F_LO_Trip_SP, and a pre-trip alarm when it falls to or below h_SG2_F_LO_Trip_SP + k_SG2_F_LO_Pretrip_Margin.

The trip setpoint h_SG2_F_LO_Trip_SP shall track f_SG2_F - k_SG2_F_LO_Band limited to [k_SG2_F_LO_SP_Min, k_SG2_F_LO_SP_Max].  It shall follow increasing flow without delay and shall decrease at no more than k_SG2_F_LO_SP_Rate, so that a rapid flow reduction produces a trip.  At start-up it shall be initialised from the first valid input.
The Low Reactor Coolant Flow (SG2 loop) trip may be placed in operating bypass (f_SG2_F_LO_OB_Ini) while the low-power permissive is present (f_NPWR_LOG < k_LP_OB_Perm).
